title: Erikson psychosocial stages
clinicalContext: Hospitalized 2-y-old clinging to parent, resists strangers.
nursingPriority: Age-appropriate autonomy vs shame — encourage autonomy in age-appropriate care, parent presence, predictable routine.

title: Ego defense mechanisms
keyPoints: Neurotic: repression, displacement, reaction formation, intellectualization
Immature: denial, projection, regression, acting out, somatization, splitting
clinicalContext: Recently divorced man blames ex for his alcoholism.
nursingPriority: Identify projection; psychotherapy — explore feelings, identify healthier coping, refer to counselor.

title: Psychoanalytic theory — Freud
keyPoints: Fixation at a stage → adult pathology
clinicalContext: Item on stage associated with toilet training conflicts.
nursingPriority: Identify anal stage (1-3 y).

title: Freud structural theory of mind (id/ego/superego)
keyPoints: Superego: morals, ideals, internalized parental values
clinicalContext: Patient repeatedly steals despite guilt.
nursingPriority: Id-superego conflict; therapy to address underlying drives.

title: Delirium
definition: Acute disturbance of consciousness and cognition.
keyPoints: Abrupt onset, fluctuating course, inattention, disorganized thinking, altered LOC
Causes: infection, drugs, electrolyte, hypoxia, pain, restraint, sleep deprivation
Treatment: address cause, reorient, minimize restraints, low-dose haloperidol only if severely agitated
clinicalContext: Post-op elderly with fluctuating confusion, pulling lines.
nursingPriority: Screen with CAM, identify cause (infection, meds, pain, dehydration, hypoxia), non-pharmacologic first (reorientation, family, sleep, lighting), low-dose haloperidol only if severe agitation.

title: Delirium vs dementia
keyPoints: Delirium: acute, fluctuating, reversible, LOC altered, attention impaired
Dementia: chronic, stable, irreversible, LOC clear until late, memory primary
Dementia can be complicated by delirium
clinicalContext: Elderly with 2-day confusion on background of Alzheimer.
nursingPriority: Suspect superimposed delirium — full workup for reversible causes, avoid restraints.

title: Parkinson disease — psych features
keyPoints: Treatment: SSRIs for depression; clozapine/pimavanserin for psychosis (avoid typical antipsychotics)
clinicalContext: Parkinson patient with visual hallucinations.
nursingPriority: Review dopaminergic dose, consider clozapine or pimavanserin; avoid haloperidol (EPS worsens).

title: Extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS)
keyPoints: Acute dystonia: minutes-hours — IM diphenhydramine or benztropine
Parkinsonism: bradykinesia, rigidity — reduce dose, anticholinergic
Tardive dyskinesia: late, irreversible — switch to atypical, VMAT2 inhibitor
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: life-threatening — stop drug, cooling, dantrolene
clinicalContext: Schizophrenia patient on haloperidol with torticollis and oculogyric crisis.
nursingPriority: Acute dystonia — IM diphenhydramine 50 mg or benztropine 1-2 mg; reassurance; review antipsychotic choice.

title: Vascular dementia
keyPoints: Stepwise cognitive decline with each stroke
MRI: multiple infarcts, white matter disease
clinicalContext: Stepwise memory decline with multiple strokes on MRI.
nursingPriority: Optimize vascular risk factors (BP, DM, statin, aspirin), rehabilitation, treat depression, avoid benzodiazepines.

title: Bender-Gestalt test
keyPoints: Copy 9 designs; score for errors, distortions
Useful in organic brain syndrome screen, learning disability
Not specific for a single disorder
clinicalContext: Item on projective vs objective.
nursingPriority: Bender-Gestalt is a projective/visuomotor test.

title: Antipsychotic medications — side effects
keyPoints: Typical (haloperidol, chlorpromazine, fluphenazine): high D2 block — EPS risk
Atypical (risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, clozapine, aripiprazole): broader receptor — metabolic side effects
Clozapine: refractory schizophrenia; agranulocytosis (weekly CBC first 6 mo)
clinicalContext: Schizophrenia on olanzapine gains 10 kg.
nursingPriority: Metabolic side effect — lifestyle counseling, monitor lipids/FBS, consider switching to aripiprazole if severe.

title: Tricyclic antidepressants — side effects
definition: TCAs — serotonin + NE reuptake block + anticholinergic.
keyPoints: Side effects: dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, widened QRS, sedation
Overdose dangerous — seizures, arrhythmia; sodium bicarbonate antidote (QRS wide)
clinicalContext: TCA overdose with wide QRS 140 ms, seizure.
nursingPriority: Sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV bolus, continuous cardiac monitoring, control seizure with benzodiazepine, avoid procainamide.

title: Chlorpromazine (Thorazine) side effects
keyPoints: Side effects: sedation, orthostatic hypotension, photosensitivity, cholestatic jaundice, EPS
clinicalContext: Patient on chlorpromazine complains of severe sun burn.
nursingPriority: Photosensitivity — sun protection, hat, sunscreen, consider alternative antipsychotic.

title: Clozapine — monitoring (WBC)
definition: Atypical for refractory schizophrenia; most effective.
keyPoints: Agranulocytosis risk — weekly CBC x6 mo, then biweekly, then monthly; stop if ANC <1500
clinicalContext: Patient on clozapine with sore throat and fever.
nursingPriority: Check ANC urgently — discontinue if agranulocytosis (<1500), protective isolation, blood cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics.

title: MAO inhibitors — tyramine interactions
keyPoints: Hypertensive crisis with tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, wine, smoked meats, soy)
clinicalContext: Depression on phenelzine develops severe headache after cheese.
nursingPriority: Hypertensive crisis — IV phentolamine or nitroprusside, monitor BP, ICU.

title: Depression — neurotransmitter deficits
keyPoints: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs target these
clinicalContext: Item on depression biochemistry.
nursingPriority: Cite decreased 5-HT, NE, DA.

title: Types of delusion
clinicalContext: Patient insists body is rotting though healthy.
nursingPriority: Cotard (nihilistic) delusion — assess suicide risk, start antipsychotic, ECT consideration.

title: Depression vs normal grief
keyPoints: Grief: waves, preserved self-worth, identification with deceased, resolves 6-12 mo
MDD: pervasive, worthlessness, functional impairment, suicidal ideation beyond deceased
clinicalContext: Widow 6 mo after loss with worthlessness, suicidal thoughts.
nursingPriority: Consider complicated grief or MDD — screen with PHQ-9, safety assess, counseling, consider SSRI.

title: Omega sign in depression
definition: Omega-shaped furrow between eyebrows seen in severe depression.
keyPoints: Supports clinical impression but not specific
clinicalContext: Item on omega sign.
nursingPriority: Recognize as corrugator furrow in severe depression.

title: Clinical features of depression
definition: DSM-5 MDD: 5/9 symptoms for 2 wk including depressed mood or anhedonia.
keyPoints: SIGECAPS: Sleep, Interest, Guilt, Energy, Concentration, Appetite, Psychomotor, Suicide
Treatment: psychotherapy + SSRI first-line, ECT if severe/psychotic
clinicalContext: Patient with 3 wk of low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, weight loss, worthlessness, suicidal ideation.
nursingPriority: MDD — safety assess (hospitalize if active suicidality), start SSRI (sertraline), schedule psychotherapy, close follow-up.

title: Lithium — serum levels and toxicity
clinicalContext: Bipolar on lithium with tremor and diarrhea.
nursingPriority: Check level, stop offending drugs, hydrate.

title: Bipolar disorder
keyPoints: Treatment: lithium, valproate (not pregnancy), lamotrigine, atypical antipsychotics; avoid antidepressant monotherapy
clinicalContext: Patient with 1 wk of grandiosity, reduced sleep need, rapid speech.
nursingPriority: Mania — hospital admission for safety, start mood stabilizer (lithium or valproate) + atypical antipsychotic, educate about sleep hygiene and relapse signs.

title: Manic-depressive disorder
definition: Historical name for bipolar disorder. See Mental-22.
clinicalContext: Same as bipolar.
nursingPriority: Treat per bipolar guidelines.

title: Types of hallucinations
clinicalContext: Alcoholic 36 h withdrawal with feeling of bugs crawling on skin.
nursingPriority: Tactile (formication) — benzodiazepine per CIWA, thiamine, reassure, address underlying withdrawal.

title: Negative vs positive symptoms (schizophrenia)
keyPoints: Positive: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, catatonia
Negative: flat affect, alogia, avolition, anhedonia, asociality
clinicalContext: Item on positive symptoms.
nursingPriority: Identify as added behaviors (hallucinations, delusions).

title: Bleuler 4 As of schizophrenia
clinicalContext: Item on Bleuler.
nursingPriority: Recall the 4 As.

title: CAGE questionnaire
clinicalContext: Patient admits drinking 6 drinks/day.
nursingPriority: Administer CAGE; if >=2 positive, full assessment for AUD and intervention.

title: Cannabis (sativa) effects
keyPoints: Acute: euphoria, red eyes, dry mouth, tachycardia, impaired memory
Chronic: amotivational syndrome, psychosis risk, pulmonary
clinicalContext: Young adult with new-onset psychosis after heavy marijuana use.
nursingPriority: Admit, urine toxicology, rule out organic cause, cessation support, risperidone if psychotic.

title: Chronic alcoholism — complications
keyPoints: GI: esophageal varices, pancreatitis, cirrhosis, Mallory-Weiss
Neuro: Wernicke, Korsakoff, peripheral neuropathy, cerebellar degeneration
clinicalContext: Chronic alcoholic with confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia.
nursingPriority: Wernicke encephalopathy — IV thiamine 500 mg TDS x3 d before glucose, magnesium, supportive care.

title: Alcohol withdrawal symptoms
clinicalContext: Same as Pharma-41.
nursingPriority: CIWA-triggered benzodiazepine.

title: Korsakoff psychosis
definition: Irreversible chronic amnestic disorder from thiamine deficiency.
keyPoints: Prevention: thiamine in alcoholics before glucose
clinicalContext: Chronic alcoholic with confabulation and memory gaps.
nursingPriority: Thiamine 100 mg IV TDS x3 d, then oral, cognitive rehabilitation, social services, abstinence support.

title: Delirium tremens
keyPoints: Autonomic hyperactivity: HR/BP high, fever, diaphoresis
Treatment: IV benzodiazepines (diazepam/lorazepam), thiamine, fluids, ICU if needed
clinicalContext: 72 h post-admission alcoholic with agitation, fever 39, visual hallucinations.
nursingPriority: Admit ICU/HDU, IV lorazepam per CIWA titration, thiamine IV, fluids, monitor electrolytes/Mg, sitter/restraints if needed.

title: Opioid dependence
keyPoints: Withdrawal (not life-threatening): yawning, rhinorrhea, lacrimation, piloerection, cramps, diarrhea, mydriasis
Treatment: methadone or buprenorphine maintenance, naltrexone, counseling
clinicalContext: Heroin user wants treatment.
nursingPriority: Refer to OST clinic for buprenorphine/methadone, counseling, HIV/HCV screening, harm reduction education.

title: Codeine
definition: Weak opioid; metabolized to morphine via CYP2D6.
keyPoints: Dose 30-60 mg for pain; antitussive at lower dose
Ultra-rapid metabolizers risk of respiratory depression
clinicalContext: Child after tonsillectomy.
nursingPriority: Avoid codeine in children post-T&A; use non-opioid or other opioid cautiously.

title: Conversion disorder
keyPoints: Motor/sensory symptoms not explained by organic disease
Diagnostic criteria: positive signs of inconsistency
Treatment: supportive, avoid reinforcement, physical therapy, CBT
clinicalContext: Woman with sudden unilateral paralysis after argument, normal MRI, variable weakness on exam.
nursingPriority: Rule out organic cause, reassure, involve PT/OT, CBT, avoid invasive tests; validate symptoms without reinforcement.

title: Phobia — types
definition: Persistent fear of object/situation out of proportion to real threat.
keyPoints: Treatment: CBT with exposure + response prevention, SSRI for social anxiety
clinicalContext: Patient avoids flying due to intense fear.
nursingPriority: CBT with graded exposure, consider short-term benzo for acute flight, SSRI if disabling.

title: Somatoform disorder
keyPoints: Persistent physical symptoms with excessive thoughts/feelings about health
Treatment: regular scheduled visits with one provider, CBT, antidepressants
clinicalContext: Patient with 10-year history of multiple medical workups, no findings.
nursingPriority: Establish therapeutic alliance, regular scheduled visits, validate symptoms, minimize repeated investigations, CBT referral.

title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
keyPoints: Treatment: CBT with exposure and response prevention, SSRI (higher doses than depression — fluoxetine 40-80 mg), clomipramine
clinicalContext: Patient washes hands 3 h daily.
nursingPriority: SSRI (fluoxetine 40 mg) + CBT with ERP; support family education; monitor response over 8-12 wk.

title: Eating disorders — anorexia vs bulimia
keyPoints: Anorexia: BMI <17.5, intense fear of weight gain, restriction, amenorrhea
Bulimia: binge + purge, normal/over-weight, Russell sign, dental erosion
clinicalContext: 16-y-old BMI 15 with amenorrhea and fear of weight gain.
nursingPriority: Admit if medically unstable; slow refeeding to avoid refeeding syndrome, CBT, family therapy, SSRI for comorbid depression.

title: Autism spectrum disorder
definition: Neurodevelopmental: social communication deficits + restricted repetitive behaviors by age 3.
keyPoints: No cure; early intervention (ABA, speech, OT) improves outcomes
clinicalContext: 3-y-old with delayed speech, no pointing, repetitive behaviors.
nursingPriority: Refer for formal diagnostic evaluation (ADOS), start early intervention (speech + ABA), parent training, rule out hearing loss.

title: Psychotic disorders — distinguishing features
keyPoints: Schizophrenia: >=6 mo with 2+ of 5 features including 1 positive
clinicalContext: Patient with 3 wk of hallucinations without mood episode.
nursingPriority: Schizophreniform (if <6 mo); start atypical antipsychotic, monitor, reassess at 6 mo.

title: REM and NREM sleep stages
keyPoints: REM: dreaming, muscle atonia, autonomic variability
clinicalContext: Item on dreaming stage.
nursingPriority: REM sleep is the dreaming stage with muscle atonia.

title: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
definition: Electrical induction of generalized seizure under anesthesia.
keyPoints: Indications: severe MDD, catatonia, treatment-resistant, psychotic depression, suicidality
Contraindication: recent MI, raised ICP, severe cardiac disease (relative)
Side effects: transient memory impairment, headache, muscle aches
Consent essential; bilateral more effective, unilateral less cognitive impact
clinicalContext: Severe depression with food refusal, resistant to medications.
nursingPriority: ECT indicated — consult psychiatry, informed consent, pre-anesthesia clearance, baseline MMSE, post-ECT monitoring.

title: Cognitive behavioral therapy
definition: Structured time-limited psychotherapy focused on thoughts, feelings, behaviors.
keyPoints: Core: identify cognitive distortions, behavioral activation, exposure
Evidence-based for depression, anxiety, OCD, PTSD, insomnia
clinicalContext: Mild-moderate MDD patient prefers non-pharmacologic treatment.
nursingPriority: Refer for CBT 12-16 sessions, monitor PHQ-9 q2-4 wk, add SSRI if inadequate response.
